provenance.source: AIT Log Data Set V2.0 (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.5789064, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), scenario russellmitchell; per-line labels from the dataset's labels/ directory, carried by the adapters into labels.jsonl.
provenance.incident_window: Labelled intrusion events span 2022-01-24 03:01:00 (VPN login with jhall's certificate) to 04:38:06 (sudo cat /etc/shadow as jhall), matching the dataset's attack timeline. The interval is widened to window boundaries: 03:00-04:40. The builder checks that every incident-class event falls inside it.
provenance.label_classes: Every label observed in the converted sources is mapped. 'incident' = the multi-step intrusion (VPN foothold, DNS/network/service scans, dirb, wpscan, webshell upload and commands, su to jhall, sudo). 'exfiltration' = DNSteal traffic from one internal host. An unmapped label stops the build.
provenance.ignored_labels: 'attacker' is an umbrella label that, in this slice, sits only on the DNSteal lines (17,693 of 17,693); the class comes from the dnsteal* labels instead.
provenance.exfiltration_overlaps_training: DNSteal is labelled from the first minute of the data (2022-01-21 00:00:09) to 2022-01-24 13:52:15, so it is present in baseline, train and validation. There is no clean pre-exfiltration period. It is a separate class, never the incident under test. Two variants are built: 'as-is' (baseline fitted on everything in the baseline split, as an unsupervised system would see it) and 'clean-baseline' (exfiltration-class events removed from the baseline fit using the labels - disclosed, optimistic for exfiltration).
provenance.splits: Time-ordered. baseline (Jan 21): fit the baseline only. train (Jan 22): fit unsupervised models. validation (Jan 23 00-23h): calibrate thresholds on background windows. gap (Jan 23 23-24h): excluded. test (Jan 24): the intrusion, the end of the exfiltration, and ~19 h afterwards. Web traffic starts at 05:55 on Jan 21, so the baseline sees under a day of web activity.
provenance.seen_before_evaluation: The attack timeline and label names were read to write this spec. Detector design (rules-1.1.0 calibration change) was decided on Org Y before any AIT detector output was looked at.
